newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group says agrees with Turkey on border.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group says agrees with Turkey on border.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said on Monday it had reached a tentative agreement with Turkey to repopulate villages along the Turkish-Iraqi border to guard against Turkish Kurd rebel attacks.

"The Turkish authorities have slowly come round to our point of view on the issue and have agreed in principle over the matter of the villages," Safeen Dizayee, Ankara spokesman for the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), told Reuters.

Turkey's Yeni Yuzyil daily said the KDP had asked Ankara for economic support to rehabit up to 400 abandoned villages on the Iraqi side of the mountainous border in a bid to prevent Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas operating in the area.
The PKK uses both sides of the border in its fight for self-rule in southeastern Turkey and often clashes with the Iraqi Kurdish militia, led by Massoud Barzani.

"We need to repopulate the villages for security reasons...Experience shows a depopulated area can be more harmful than a populated area and the villages can be a substantial force to protect the border," Dizayee said.
The villages lie empty as a result of deportations by the Baghdad government in the 1970s and 1980s and fighting between the PKK and the Turkish army in recent years.
Turkey has previously opposed the repopulation of the border to give itself a free rein in its fight against the PKK.
Turkey's foreign ministry said there was no definite deal to repopulate the area.

"Turkey in the past extended a considerable amount of humanitarian assistance to the people in northern Iraq. In the future, in what specific shape this aid will continue remains to be seen. There is nothing concrete at the present," spokesman Sermet Aracanli told a news conference.
"There are demands on that issue by all parties," Atacanli said when asked if Turkey would give economic support to the KDP for the repopulation drive.
Barzani's group joined forces with the Turkish army in May in an incursion into northern Iraq against the PKK.

Turkey said almost all its troops left northern Iraq in June but Turkish newspapers said on Monday a Turkish tank unit was stationed at Fayshabur on Iraq's border with Syria to guard against any PKK infiltration into the area from Syria.
